records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:500 — The installer check is bypassed when the webhook has not yet created the Integration, allowing any OAuth-authenticated user with its installation ID to attach the victim installation through the earlier next_step branch.
records.rationale: The finding identifies a real security issue. Looking at line 481 in the diff, when `Integration.DoesNotExist` is caught, the code calls `return pipeline.next_step()` without any ownership verification. At this point, the `github_authenticated_user` has been bound to pipeline state (from OAuthLoginView), but the ownership check (comparing `github_authenticated_user` to `integration.metadata['sender']['login']`) only happens AFTER the try/except block when the Integration DOES exist (lines 493-500). records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — Token exchange transport failures escape the try block and turn transient GitHub outages into an unhandled installation failure instead of the failure dialog.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in OAuthLoginView.dispatch(), the call to safe_urlopen() at line 423 and get_user_info() at line 432 are not wrapped in try/except blocks. Looking at the diff, the only exception handling is around safe_urlread() (lines 425-428), but if safe_urlopen() itself raises a connection exception, or if get_user_info() raises an HTTP exception, these would propagate up and abort the setup callback without rendering the failure dialog.
